title: Symphony No. 41 in C major, “Jupiter”
hook: Mozart’s last symphony, ending in a finale where five tunes play at once.

painting.title: The Obelisk
painting.pairingNote: Painted a year before the symphony, it builds a vast, ordered space out of the columns and vaults of ancient Rome, with the same grandeur and the same calm Classical balance.

facts: Mozart entered the symphony in his own catalogue of works on 10 August 1788. It is the last of three symphonies he wrote that summer, after No. 39 (June) and No. 40 (July), and the last symphony he ever wrote.

Nobody knows for certain whether Mozart heard it performed. The nickname “Jupiter” is not his: according to his son, it was probably coined by the London concert manager Johann Peter Salomon, and it was in use in London early in the 19th century.
The orchestra has trumpets and drums, which give the outer movements their ceremonial, festive sound. There are no clarinets.
The finale is famous for its ending: five short tunes, each heard separately before, are played at the same time.
bigPicture.inOneLine: power and grace side by side (I), a hushed song with dark undercurrents (II), a gliding dance (III), a finale that weaves five tunes together (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro vivace
movements.summary: A grand, confident opening movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]. Loud ceremonial passages with trumpets and drums alternate with quiet, graceful ones, and near the end of the exposition Mozart slips in a light tune from one of his own comic arias.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1, power and grace
mainIdeas.description: three loud hammer-strokes from the whole orchestra, answered by a soft, gentle phrase in the strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a calm, singing melody in the strings, in G major.

mainIdeas.name: The aria tune
mainIdeas.description: a light, tripping melody in the violins, borrowed from *Un bacio di mano*, a song Mozart had written a few months earlier for a comic opera singer.

stops.hear: Three loud, emphatic strokes from the full orchestra, then a soft reply in the strings; then the pattern again
stops.happening: Theme 1. The contrast of force and grace runs through the whole movement

stops.hear: After a pause, a gentle, flowing melody in the strings
A sudden loud outburst from the whole orchestra, in the minor
stops.happening: A storm in the middle of the second theme group

stops.hear: A light, chattering tune in the violins, almost like a comic song
stops.happening: The aria tune from *Un bacio di mano* closes the [[exposition|exposition]]

stops.hear: The three loud strokes again
Woodwinds slide down together, and the aria tune returns in a new key
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins, built at first on the aria tune

stops.hear: The opening tune comes back quietly, but sounds slightly wrong
stops.happening: A false return: the theme appears in the “wrong” key, F major, before the music moves on

stops.hear: The three loud strokes in the home key

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The aria tune once more, then fanfares from trumpets and drums
stops.happening: The movement ends in full ceremonial C major

notice: The movement keeps switching between loud and soft, often within a few seconds. Listen for which instruments drop out when the music goes quiet.
The comic aria tune at about 2:40 is light and almost silly, yet in the development it becomes the main material.

movements.heading: Andante cantabile
movements.summary: A slow, songlike movement for [[muted|muted]] violins, in the rhythm of a stately dance in three. The surface is calm, but twice the music turns suddenly dark and restless. Trumpets and drums are silent here.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a slow, dignified melody on muted violins, which gives it a soft, veiled sound.

mainIdeas.name: The shadow
mainIdeas.description: restless, off-beat figures in a minor key that interrupt the calm.

stops.hear: Muted violins play a slow, stately melody; the rest of the strings support it
stops.happening: The main theme. “Cantabile” means in a singing style

stops.hear: The mood darkens: uneasy chords that seem to fall between the beats, in the minor
stops.happening: A sudden turn to C minor, with [[syncopation|syncopation]]

stops.hear: A gentler, singing idea
stops.happening: The closing idea of the first half

stops.hear: The opening melody again
The restless off-beat figures return and grow stronger
The stately melody returns
The restless middle section starts again

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The opening melody once more, quietly

notice: The mutes make the violins sound distant. Compare their tone with the loud, open strings of the first movement.

movements.heading: Menuetto: Allegretto
movements.summary: A [[minuet|minuet]] that glides rather than stamps. Its main tune falls gently step by step, and the whole orchestra answers with loud, festive chords. The [[trio|trio]] contains a small preview of the finale.

stops.hear: Violins play a gently falling, sliding line; the whole orchestra answers

stops.label: Second half of the minuet
stops.hear: Woodwinds alone pass a short falling phrase from one instrument to the next
stops.happening: Imitation in the winds, a quiet moment before the full orchestra returns

stops.hear: The music lightens: short, quiet phrases in the woodwinds and strings

stops.label: Second half of the trio
stops.hear: A four-note figure, rising and falling, in the minor
stops.happening: The four-note figure that will become the main theme of the finale

stops.hear: The gliding minuet returns
stops.happening: The minuet is played again, without repeats

notice: Keep the four-note figure from the trio in your ear. It opens the next movement.

movements.heading: Molto allegro
movements.summary: A fast finale in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] that is also a showcase of [[counterpoint|counterpoint]]: Mozart builds it from five short themes and keeps combining them. At the very end, all five are heard at once.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: four long, quiet notes in the violins (C, D, F, E), followed by a quick, lively answer.

mainIdeas.name: Four companions
mainIdeas.description: short figures, each with its own clear rhythm, which Mozart introduces one by one.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, graceful tune in G major.

stops.hear: Violins softly play four long notes, then a quick answer; soon the whole orchestra bursts in
The four-note theme enters in one string section after another, piling up
A gentler, graceful tune
The four long notes again
The four-note theme in minor keys, tossed between high and low instruments
The four long notes return in the home key
The stormy development again
Quiet again: the four-note theme, now passed between instruments
Layer after layer: five different themes enter and play together
stops.happening: The five themes combined, in five-part counterpoint

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Fanfares with trumpets and drums
stops.happening: The symphony ends in festive C major

notice: At about 10:45, try to follow one theme while the others go on around it. Then try to hear them all at once.
The four long notes are slow, but the music around them never stops racing. That contrast of slow and fast runs through the whole movement.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Mackerras plays every repeat Mozart wrote, including the second-half repeats in the Andante and the finale that many conductors leave out. That is why these two movements last more than ten minutes each.

threads.title: Power and grace
threads.body: The first movement sets loud, ceremonial music against quiet, delicate music. The finale ends the symphony in the same contrast.

threads.title: Four notes
threads.body: The four-note figure in the trio of the minuet becomes the main theme of the finale.

threads.title: Learned and light
threads.body: Mozart builds the finale on strict counterpoint, yet the music stays quick and lively throughout.
